Detailed Requirement: Provide authorized administrators with the ability to manage SystemPrompt users directly from the Admin UI, including viewing/searching, creating, updating, disabling/deleting users, assigning roles, viewing last login, and revoking sessions.
Business Value / Rationale: Centralized administration is required before SystemPrompt can move beyond a controlled evaluation environment.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin can search/list users, create users, modify role/status, disable/delete access, review basic account activity, and revoke sessions without CLI or database access.
Current Assessment: Delivered: full user CRUD, role/status edit, disable/delete, invites, session + PAT revocation, last-active - all in the Admin UI. Three security defects fixed alongside (role-escalation guard, cross-org enumeration, search box).
SystemPrompt Fit: Backend/CLI capability appears available; Admin UI exposure needs validation.
Gap / Action Required: Confirm current Admin UI capability and expose/enable existing user-management functions.
Validation Method: Admin UI functional test + role-based access test
Ed's comments: Delivered - please test against the latest deployment. Evidence: @REQ-001 Playwright specs + screenshots in requirements/evidence/.

Detailed Requirement: Prevent unrestricted self-registration. Only approved users should be eligible to create/use SystemPrompt accounts and connect a Bridge.
Business Value / Rationale: Open registration is an enterprise access-control risk and must be hardened before broader rollout.
Acceptance Criteria: An unapproved user cannot create an account or connect a Bridge. Approved/provisioned users can access the platform based on assigned entitlements.
Current Assessment: Delivered: enrolment closed on all three doors (core allow_registration, passkey self-reg, SSO auto-provision). Admin invite (single-use, 7-day TTL) is the only path in.
SystemPrompt Fit: Authentication and role controls exist; enterprise enrolment policy is not clearly documented.
Gap / Action Required: Define and implement closed enrolment; confirm admin provisioning, allowlists, SSO/domain restrictions, or equivalent controls.
Validation Method: Negative registration test + approved-user onboarding test
Notes: Current dev setup allows self-registration for testing.
Ed's comments: Delivered. Trade-off accepted per requirement: every new user needs an admin invite. Open question: should Bridge device-link also need per-device admin approval?

Detailed Requirement: Provide an Admin dashboard showing SystemPrompt usage trends, request volumes, active users, and daily/weekly activity.
Business Value / Rationale: Required to understand platform adoption, operational usage, and overall utilization.
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard shows daily/weekly requests, total request volume, active users, and historical usage trends with selectable time periods.
Current Assessment: Delivered: 5-tab SSR analytics dashboard - request volume, error rate, active users, daily/weekly series, selectable periods 15m-30d + custom.
SystemPrompt Fit: Analytics capability is documented, but required views are not visible in the current Astound deployment.
Gap / Action Required: Confirm deployment/version/configuration and expose the documented analytics in the Admin UI.
Ed's comments: Delivered. Note: 30-day ceiling on custom windows - confirm whether quarter/year views are required (query-cost decision).

Detailed Requirement: Provide visibility into total AI spend, daily cost trends, cost per request, request counters, and AI model usage distribution.
Business Value / Rationale: Enables cost governance, model optimization, and identification of major cost drivers.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin can see total spend, spend trend, cost/request, token/request activity, and usage distribution by AI model.
Current Assessment: Delivered: total spend, daily cost trend, cost/request, token counters, model distribution, cost-by-model series, month-end P&L by org/provider/model.
SystemPrompt Fit: Core request, token, model, and cost telemetry appears available.
Gap / Action Required: Validate available fields and configure/build the required Admin dashboard visualizations.
Validation Method: Compare dashboard totals with request/cost telemetry
Ed's comments: Delivered. Costs are integer microdollars end to end; reconcile dashboard totals against `systemprompt analytics costs summary`.

Detailed Requirement: Provide user-level analytics including active seats/users, weekly active users, requests per user/day, top users, and users with zero requests over a configurable period such as 30 days.
Business Value / Rationale: Allows identification of adoption gaps, under-utilized access, and potentially wasted seats/capacity.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin can report WAU, requests/user/day, top users, and inactive users over a configurable period.
Current Assessment: Delivered: WAU with deltas, requests/user/day, top-user leaderboard, inactive seats with configurable window (7/14/30/90 days).
SystemPrompt Fit: Underlying user-attributed request data appears available; some KPIs are likely derived rather than standard widgets.
Gap / Action Required: Validate available reporting and add derived widgets/queries where required.
Validation Method: User-level analytics reconciliation against raw request logs
Ed's comments: Delivered. 'Never used' is now distinguishable from 'used on day one' (last_active is nullable).

Detailed Requirement: Allow usage, cost, and adoption analytics to be filtered and aggregated by team/group, individual user, Hub, and potentially project.
Business Value / Rationale: Astound needs to compare usage and cost across Core, Commerce, projects, teams, and individual users.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin can filter and aggregate analytics by organizational dimension and drill down to user-level detail.
Current Assessment: Org, department and individual-user drill-down applied identically across all dashboards. Team/Hub/project dimensions do not exist.
SystemPrompt Fit: User attribution exists, but an enterprise organizational hierarchy is not clearly documented.
Gap / Action Required: Confirm native metadata dimensions; if missing, define Hub/project/team metadata and reporting model.
Validation Method: Metadata model test + filtered analytics validation
Ed's comments: Blocked on Astound defining 'Hub' (nesting, membership, entitlement vs label). Design + estimate ready in requirements/design-org-hierarchy-and-scm.md - 1-2 wks once defined.

Detailed Requirement: Track engineering-specific metrics such as AI suggestion/Tab acceptance rate, total AI accepts, AI-generated LOC versus manual LOC, and related development activity.
Business Value / Rationale: Helps assess measurable engineering impact rather than AI consumption alone.
Acceptance Criteria: Required productivity events can be captured, attributed to users/projects, trended over time, and compared with delivery outcomes.
Current Assessment: AI-authored LOC, applied edits, permission-grant rate and commit lines shipped, labelled as proxies. Tab-acceptance rate has no data source - Claude Code emits no accept/reject signal.
SystemPrompt Fit: IDE-level acceptance and AI-versus-manual LOC telemetry is not clearly documented as native gateway telemetry.
Gap / Action Required: Confirm Bridge/IDE telemetry capabilities; otherwise define IDE/SCM telemetry integration.
Validation Method: IDE event capture test + repository attribution test
Notes: Tab acceptance benchmark requested by stakeholder should be treated as a metric target, not a native SystemPrompt capability.
Ed's comments: Not feasible as specified on this platform; needs an IDE-level integration to ever exist. Treat the acceptance-rate benchmark as a metric target, not a platform capability.

Detailed Requirement: Provide daily/weekly commit activity alongside AI usage to support correlation between AI consumption and engineering activity.
Business Value / Rationale: Provides contextual engineering activity data when assessing AI adoption and productivity.
Acceptance Criteria: Commit activity can be viewed for the same user/team/project/time period as SystemPrompt AI usage.
Current Assessment: Commits observed through Claude Code sessions captured, deduped, rolled up daily, plotted beside AI usage. Commits outside Claude Code invisible.
SystemPrompt Fit: Commit data originates from Git/SCM systems rather than the AI gateway.
Gap / Action Required: Integrate GitHub/Bitbucket/Git telemetry or ingest commit metrics into the analytics layer.
Validation Method: SCM integration test + identity matching validation
Notes: Commit count should be contextual, not used as a standalone productivity KPI.
Ed's comments: Blocked on Astound nominating the authoritative SCM + identity mapping (SCM login -> platform user). Webhook ingest is straightforward once decided (~1 wk).

Detailed Requirement: Display proximity to defined soft/hard AI spend limits and support monitoring and alerting for budget consumption.
Business Value / Rationale: Prevents uncontrolled AI spend and supports predictable enterprise financial governance.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin can see current spend versus budget, threshold utilization, and alerts/actions when configured limits are reached.
Current Assessment: Delivered and enforced: hard org monthly cap (429 at gateway), soft threshold recorded + Slack alert on first crossing, spend meters, burn-up chart, 12-month history.
SystemPrompt Fit: Budget/alert foundations appear available; required scope and granularity need validation.
Gap / Action Required: Validate global versus user/team/project thresholds and define any missing budget-control model.
Validation Method: Threshold alert test + spend-limit enforcement test
Ed's comments: Delivered. Budgets are per-organization; per-team/project awaits the Hub decision (REQ-006).

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to track AI spend per team, department, product or project in real time for billing accuracy, so that cost is attributed to the correct P&L owner
Business Value / Rationale: Cost is attributed to the correct P&L owner.
Acceptance Criteria: For each AI request, cost can be attributed and reported in near real time by an agreed organizational dimension such as team, department, product, project, user, model, and provider.
Current Assessment: Every request attributed with user, organization, department, model, provider, cost in near real time; dashboards and reports slice on all of them.
SystemPrompt Fit: Request/audit data includes user, tenant, model, provider, and cost. Team/department/project attribution requires a reliable custom metadata convention because department is not first-class in current code.
Gap / Action Required: Define required organizational metadata (team/department/product/project) and validate cost attribution end to end.
Validation Method: Cost attribution query + organizational metadata reconciliation
Ed's comments: Delivered for org/department/user/model/provider. Team/product/project = same Hub decision as REQ-006.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to track AI spend per team, department, product or project in real time for early-warning control, so that budget owners can detect overruns before invoice time when corrective action is no longer possible
Business Value / Rationale: Budget owners can detect overruns before invoice time when corrective action is no longer possible.
Acceptance Criteria: Budget owners can identify current spend and receive an actionable early-warning signal before the accounting period closes when spend is trending beyond the expected level.
Current Assessment: Delivered this pass: linear month-end projection computed continuously; first projected-overrun crossing per org per month is recorded and alerted to Slack.
SystemPrompt Fit: Real-time cost data exists, but the source analysis did not find spend-trajectory forecasting or proactive forecast-based notification.
Gap / Action Required: Design/confirm forecast-based budget early-warning logic and notification mechanism.
Ed's comments: New in this delivery - projection is linear run-rate, stated as such. Please test with a simulated burn.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to set and enforce soft budget alerts per team, department, product or project, so that budget owners are notified before a limit is reached without disrupting production service
Business Value / Rationale: Budget owners are notified before a limit is reached without disrupting production service.
Acceptance Criteria: A configurable soft threshold can be set for an agreed scope and triggers an alert without blocking production traffic.
Current Assessment: Soft threshold per org plan, non-blocking, Slack alert on the transition (not per request), 12-month crossing history in the UI.
SystemPrompt Fit: Documentation indicates budget alerts; code confirms quota enforcement, but a non-blocking owner notification path such as email/webhook was not evidenced.
Gap / Action Required: Confirm non-blocking soft alert channels and scope; add email/webhook/dashboard alerting if missing.
Ed's comments: Delivered. Alert channel is Slack; email/webhook can be added if required - say which.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to set and enforce hard budget cutoffs per team, department, product or project for non-production-facing workloads, so that no team can create unbudgeted financial exposure for the org
Business Value / Rationale: No team can create unbudgeted financial exposure for the org.
Acceptance Criteria: A configurable hard threshold can be set for an agreed scope and blocks further eligible AI consumption when the limit is reached.
Current Assessment: Dollar-based monthly hard cap per organization plan, enforced with 429 + retry-after at month boundary.
SystemPrompt Fit: Quota windows can enforce request/token ceilings, but the source analysis did not evidence team/project dollar-budget cutoffs.
Gap / Action Required: Define budget scope model and implement dollar-based hard cutoffs where required.
Ed's comments: Delivered at org scope. Team/project scope awaits Hub decision (REQ-006).

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to receive alerts when spend trajectories exceed forecast before the period closes (burndown forecasting), so that budget owners can intervene mid-cycle rather than discovering overrun retroactively
Business Value / Rationale: Budget owners can intervene mid-cycle rather than discovering overrun retroactively.
Acceptance Criteria: The platform projects period-end spend from current burn rate and alerts when projected spend exceeds the configured budget/forecast.
Current Assessment: Delivered this pass: burn-up chart paired with projection-vs-cap early-warning alert before period close.
SystemPrompt Fit: No period-end spend forecast or burndown projection capability was evidenced.
Gap / Action Required: Add spend forecasting/burndown capability or integrate an external FinOps analytics layer.
Ed's comments: New in this delivery (same mechanism as REQ-011).

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to generate self-service, on-demand cost reports sliced by team, department, product, project, model, or provider over any date range, so that budget owners and finance can answer ad hoc spend questions without filing a request to engineering
Business Value / Rationale: Budget owners and finance can answer ad hoc spend questions without filing a request to engineering.
Acceptance Criteria: Authorized users can generate cost reports for any supported date range and slice them by the required organizational and model dimensions without engineering support.
Current Assessment: CLI reports with arbitrary date ranges + CSV export; web admin UI now has CSV export endpoints for cost/request reports, org-scoped.
SystemPrompt Fit: Cost analytics are queryable by user/tenant/model/provider; organizational slices beyond those dimensions require agreed metadata.
Gap / Action Required: Validate self-service reporting UI/API and required dimensions/date slicing.
Validation Method: Ad hoc report generation across dimensions/date ranges
Ed's comments: Delivered this pass. Slices: org, department, user, model, provider, date range. Team/project pending Hub.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to schedule recurring cost and budget-utilization digests (e.g., weekly, monthly) delivered to budget owners and finance stakeholders, so that spend visibility doesn't depend on someone remembering to check a dashboard
Business Value / Rationale: Spend visibility doesn't depend on someone remembering to check a dashboard.
Acceptance Criteria: Recurring cost/budget digests can be scheduled and delivered automatically to configured recipients at defined intervals.
Current Assessment: Scheduled digest job (weekly/monthly) delivering cost + budget-utilization summaries to Slack.
SystemPrompt Fit: Recurring scheduled delivery was not evidenced in code and requires confirmation or extension.
Gap / Action Required: Add scheduled digest capability or integrate with reporting/notification tooling.
Ed's comments: Delivered this pass via the existing Slack transport. Email delivery possible as follow-up if needed.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to compare cost across model providers for quality-normalized equivalent tasks, so that the org can identify savings opportunities
Business Value / Rationale: The org can identify savings opportunities.
Acceptance Criteria: Equivalent workloads can be compared across providers/models using cost and an agreed quality baseline.
Current Assessment: Cost/margin breakdown by provider and model in the internal report and CLI.
SystemPrompt Fit: Cost/model/provider dimensions are available. Quality-normalized comparison still requires evaluation/quality data.
Gap / Action Required: Define a quality-normalization method and expose provider/model comparison reporting.
Ed's comments: Cost side delivered. 'Quality-normalized' comparison needs an agreed quality baseline/eval set from Astound - acceptance criterion untestable without one.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to determine the optimal model for a given task to balance cost/quality/latency trade-offs, so that spend is concentrated on tasks where model capability materially affects outcome quality
Business Value / Rationale: Spend is concentrated on tasks where model capability materially affects outcome quality.
Acceptance Criteria: Routing or recommendations can identify the preferred model for a task using configurable cost, quality, and latency criteria.
Current Assessment: Declarative routing on request shape (tools/thinking/stream/token-size) + programmatic RouteSelector seam + full cost/latency telemetry.
SystemPrompt Fit: Routing and cost telemetry exist, but no fully automatic optimizer balancing quality, latency, and cost was evidenced.
Gap / Action Required: Define optimization policy and determine whether recommendation/routing logic belongs in SystemPrompt or an evaluation layer.
Ed's comments: No automatic optimizer. Recommend: define the quality baseline (REQ-017) first, then decide whether recommendation logic lives here or in an eval layer.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to eliminate redundant API calls through tenant-isolated semantic caching, so that repeated or near-identical queries reduce cost at volume without leaking one customer's cached data into another's context
Business Value / Rationale: Repeated or near-identical queries reduce cost at volume without leaking one customer's cached data into another's context.
Acceptance Criteria: Repeated or semantically equivalent requests can use a tenant-isolated cache, with no cross-tenant data leakage and measurable cache-hit savings.
Current Assessment: No semantic cache exists in the gateway. Provider prompt-caching passthrough exists but is not a tenant cache.
SystemPrompt Fit: No tenant-isolated semantic cache capability was evidenced in the source analysis.
Gap / Action Required: Evaluate build/integration of a secure tenant-isolated semantic cache.
Ed's comments: A project of its own: embeddings, similarity thresholds, tenant-isolation proof. Recommend build-vs-integrate evaluation before committing; est 4-6 wks to build.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to abstract application code from any single model provider's API, so that the org retains negotiating leverage and low switching cost rather than facing vendor lock-in
Business Value / Rationale: The org retains negotiating leverage and low switching cost rather than facing vendor lock-in.
Acceptance Criteria: Applications use a provider-neutral gateway/API so models/providers can be changed without application-layer rewrites.
Current Assessment: Provider-neutral gateway (/v1/messages + /v1/responses), 4 wire protocols, upstream_model rewrite; live Cerebras/OpenAI/Gemini redirects prove substitution without app changes.
SystemPrompt Fit: Gateway/provider abstraction is supported and reduces direct provider coupling.
Gap / Action Required: Validate provider substitution with Core/Commerce clients and document the supported compatibility contract.
Ed's comments: Delivered and in production use. Compatibility contract documented.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to define which teams and applications can access which models under which conditions, so that access decisions are centrally auditable and revocable rather than scattered across unmanaged credentials
Business Value / Rationale: Access decisions are centrally auditable and revocable rather than scattered across unmanaged credentials.
Acceptance Criteria: Central policy controls which users/teams/applications may access which models and under what conditions; decisions are auditable and revocable.
Current Assessment: gateway_route ACL grants per role/org/department enforced at the gateway (403), auditable, revocable; admin UI access matrix.
SystemPrompt Fit: Central rules/ACLs are evidenced for user/role and governed entities. Team/application policy may require metadata or additional first-class scoping.
Gap / Action Required: Define enterprise access-policy dimensions and close gaps for team/application/project scoping.
Ed's comments: Delivered. Application-level (non-user) scoping rides service accounts today; first-class app identities can be added if required.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to manage virtual keys with budget and rate-limit assignments per team or per customer without exposing raw model provider credentials, so that a leaked or misused key has bounded blast radius
Business Value / Rationale: A leaked or misused key has bounded blast radius.
Acceptance Criteria: Administrators can issue revocable virtual credentials with scoped access, rate limits, and budget constraints without exposing provider credentials.
Current Assessment: PATs/API keys are revocable with optional expiry; org budgets + quota buckets bound any key's blast radius.
SystemPrompt Fit: PATs are revocable and rate tiers exist, but there is no evidenced virtual-key object combining explicit budget and rate-limit assignment.
Gap / Action Required: Decide whether virtual keys are required; if yes, add a credential object with budget/rate-limit policy.
Ed's comments: A key is not its own governance subject (no per-key budget/rate/model scope - keys collapse to the owning user). Real fix is a core change; scoped in the design note. Confirm whether per-key policy is genuinely required given org-level bounds.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to onboard and offboard access to AI capabilities through the existing identity provider (SSO), not ad-hoc key distribution, so that access management centrally managed
Business Value / Rationale: Access management centrally managed.
Acceptance Criteria: Users are onboarded/offboarded through the enterprise identity provider; access removal in the IdP removes SystemPrompt access without manual key cleanup.
Current Assessment: Salesforce OIDC + PKCE with gated JIT provisioning; new scheduled reconciliation job: user deactivated/removed in Salesforce is disabled here with sessions + PATs revoked.
SystemPrompt Fit: OAuth2/OIDC with PKCE, WebAuthn, and session/IdP-backed access are evidenced.
Gap / Action Required: Integrate with Astound IdP and validate provisioning/deprovisioning flows.
Ed's comments: Deprovisioning delivered via reconciliation (SCIM deliberately not built - Salesforce does not push standards SCIM and Odoo has none). Revisit SCIM only if Okta/Entra fronts the instance.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to detect and block unauthorized or shadow AI usage, so that ungoverned model usage doesn't create data leakage, compliance, or cost exposure outside IT/security visibility
Business Value / Rationale: Ungoverned model usage doesn't create data leakage, compliance, or cost exposure outside IT/security visibility.
Acceptance Criteria: Unauthorized or unmanaged AI use can be detected and, where policy requires, blocked or escalated through the governed platform.
Current Assessment: Governed-side complete: model allowlist (allow_unlisted_models false), route entitlements, full audit of every governed call.
SystemPrompt Fit: Governance/audit enforcement and managed allowlists provide a foundation for detecting and restricting ungoverned use.
Gap / Action Required: Define detection coverage for direct/non-gateway AI use and determine enforcement controls outside SystemPrompt.
Validation Method: Governed vs ungoverned traffic detection test
Ed's comments: Detection of AI traffic that never touches the gateway is a network/endpoint control outside the platform - recommend egress policy at the network layer; happy to advise.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to grant time-bound or scoped access to specific models for contractors or external teams, so that external access automatically expires without relying on manual revocation discipline
Business Value / Rationale: External access automatically expires without relying on manual revocation discipline.
Acceptance Criteria: External/contractor access can be scoped and configured to expire automatically at a defined time without manual revocation.
Current Assessment: Share-token expiry + grant valid_until delivered this pass; invites, setup tokens and JWTs already time-bound; PATs support optional expiry.
SystemPrompt Fit: Token expiration/revocation exists, but no dedicated scoped time-bound entitlement lifecycle object was evidenced.
Gap / Action Required: Add explicit expiring grants/entitlements if token expiry is insufficient for contractor governance.
Ed's comments: Remaining: no forced maximum PAT lifetime policy. Confirm required contractor-access TTL and we enforce it.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to produce an immutable audit trail of every model call (who, what model, what prompt, when, what was returned), so that the org can reconstruct incidents after the fact or demostrate compliance
Business Value / Rationale: The org can reconstruct incidents after the fact or demostrate compliance.
Acceptance Criteria: Every model call produces an immutable audit record containing actor, time, model/provider, request/response lineage, policy decision, and relevant consumption metadata.
Current Assessment: Every model call lands an ai_requests row (actor, model, provider, tokens, cost, latency, trace ids) with DB-locked actor attribution; governance decisions on the same spine.
SystemPrompt Fit: AI request and governance decision records provide detailed traceable audit data.
Gap / Action Required: Validate retention, immutability, payload protection, and audit export requirements.
Ed's comments: Caveat stated honestly: append-only by convention, not WORM/hash-chained; no retention policy on ai_requests yet. Hardening options scoped - pick one if compliance requires it.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to trace end-to-end request flows across model calls, tool invocations, and downstream systems, so that root-cause analysis doesn't require manual log correlation across disconnected systems
Business Value / Rationale: Root-cause analysis doesn't require manual log correlation across disconnected systems.
Acceptance Criteria: A single trace identifier correlates the originating request, model calls, tool/MCP calls, downstream actions, outcomes, and cost.
Current Assessment: One trace id correlates request -> policy decision -> model call -> MCP/tool execution -> cost; universal chain resolver in the admin UI.
SystemPrompt Fit: Trace IDs correlate inference and tool/MCP execution, enabling end-to-end lineage.
Gap / Action Required: Run trace-lineage tests across model, MCP/tool, and downstream system calls.
Ed's comments: Delivered. Downstream (non-platform) systems join via the trace id they receive.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to feed AI telemetry into the existing observability stack (Datadog, Splunk, LGTM) via OTEL as a single standard protocol, so that AI operations are monitored with the same tooling and on-call processes as the rest of production
Business Value / Rationale: AI operations are monitored with the same tooling and on-call processes as the rest of production.
Acceptance Criteria: AI telemetry can be exported into Astound's standard observability/SIEM stack using an agreed supported protocol and mapped into existing monitoring processes.
Current Assessment: OTLP ingest (traces/logs/metrics) + live JSON audit stream over SSE + structured Postgres audit.
SystemPrompt Fit: Structured SIEM/observability export is evidenced; a distinct OTEL implementation path requires validation.
Gap / Action Required: Confirm OTEL compatibility; otherwise standardize supported JSON/SIEM export integration.
Ed's comments: No push egress to Datadog/Splunk/OTEL collector yet. Integration design scoped; tell us the target stack (Datadog? Splunk? LGTM?) and we build that exporter first (~1-2 wks).

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to report on latency SLOs per model and per use case, so that routing and provider decisions are made on measured performance rather than vendor claims
Business Value / Rationale: Routing and provider decisions are made on measured performance rather than vendor claims.
Acceptance Criteria: Latency can be reported against defined SLOs by model and use case, with sufficient data to compare providers/routes objectively.
Current Assessment: Configurable latency SLO threshold with breach reporting, p50/p95, per-model latency data (was a hardcoded 5s split).
SystemPrompt Fit: Latency is captured, but use-case SLO definition, thresholding, and SLO-specific reporting are not productized.
Gap / Action Required: Define latency SLOs and add SLO reporting/alerting by model/use-case.
Ed's comments: Delivered this pass. Per-use-case SLO taxonomy + error budgets need Astound's SLO definitions.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to apply consistent content safety guardrails (prompt injection detection, jailbreak attempts, toxic output blocking) regardless of which team built the application, so that security and brand-risk controls aren't dependent on individual team diligence
Business Value / Rationale: Security and brand-risk controls aren't dependent on individual team diligence.
Acceptance Criteria: A centrally managed safety policy is enforced consistently for all governed applications and detects/blocks agreed categories such as prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, secrets, PII, and unsafe output.
Current Assessment: Central safety chain enabled this pass: jailbreak heuristics, PII (email/credit-card/SSN/phone), secret egress scanning; buffered responses can block.
SystemPrompt Fit: Code evidences jailbreak and limited PII heuristics plus pre-dispatch blocking. Full toxicity/PII taxonomy and response-side blocking are not evidenced.
Gap / Action Required: Define required safety taxonomy and extend prompt/output guardrails beyond current heuristic coverage.
Ed's comments: Streamed responses are audit-only by design (blocking a stream mid-flight truncates). No toxicity/brand-risk classifier - sign off the category set you need blocked and we extend.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to detect anomalies in model usage patterns (volume spikes, unusual prompt structures, cost outliers), so that cost, security, or quality incidents are caught proactively rather than discovered downstream
Business Value / Rationale: Cost, security, or quality incidents are caught proactively rather than discovered downstream.
Acceptance Criteria: The platform detects configured usage anomalies such as volume spikes, error spikes, unusual behavior, or cost outliers and surfaces actionable alerts.
Current Assessment: Persisted anomaly job over cost/volume/error spikes with Slack alerts and dashboard surface (replaces core's in-memory-only engine).
SystemPrompt Fit: Code includes anomaly thresholds and trend/spike detection although this capability is not clearly surfaced in public documentation.
Gap / Action Required: Expose anomaly detection operationally and validate alert thresholds/action routing.
Ed's comments: Delivered this pass with threshold-based detection; thresholds will need tuning against real traffic in the first weeks.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to failover automatically to a secondary model provider when a primary provider is unavailable without application code changes, so that provider outages don't translate into application downtime or emergency engineering response
Business Value / Rationale: Provider outages don't translate into application downtime or emergency engineering response.
Acceptance Criteria: When the primary provider fails, eligible traffic automatically fails over to an approved secondary provider without application code changes.
Current Assessment: Correction to earlier assessment: this is a Gap, not Partial - no failover exists in the gateway dispatch path (the 'fallback' previously cited belongs to the agent AI service).
SystemPrompt Fit: Fallback/failover exists on provider errors, but proactive health-check-driven failover was not evidenced.
Gap / Action Required: Run provider-failure tests and decide whether proactive provider health checks are required.
Ed's comments: Needs secondary-provider fields on routes + error/health-triggered retry in core. Est 2-3 wks. Interim mitigation: manual route flip is a one-line profile change.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to rate-limit LLM traffic per consumer, so that one team or runaway agent cannot exhaust org-wide provider quotas or internal budgets and degrade service for everyone else
Business Value / Rationale: One team or runaway agent cannot exhaust org-wide provider quotas or internal budgets and degrade service for everyone else.
Acceptance Criteria: Rate limits can be applied per agreed consumer boundary so one user/team/agent/application cannot exhaust shared provider capacity.
Current Assessment: Quota windows (requests/tokens/cost per user and per org) configured and enabled this pass; role-tier multipliers; per-org caps.
SystemPrompt Fit: Tiered request rate limiting is supported; team/department-specific boundaries require confirmation.
Gap / Action Required: Define consumer identity/scoping and validate isolation under load.
Ed's comments: Enabled this pass - review the quota sizes we set against expected traffic. Team-level limits await Hub (REQ-006).

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to route requests to self-hosted or private cloud models for workloads that cannot leave the network boundary, so that data residency, regulatory, or security requirements are met without forgoing AI capability entirely
Business Value / Rationale: Data residency, regulatory, or security requirements are met without forgoing AI capability entirely.
Acceptance Criteria: Eligible workloads can be routed to self-hosted/private endpoints with no unintended public-provider egress.
Current Assessment: Any OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible private endpoint is a config entry; Backend surface keeps private providers un-advertised; routes validated at boot.
SystemPrompt Fit: Self-hosted/private routing and air-gapped patterns are supported.
Gap / Action Required: Validate approved private endpoints, network controls, and no-egress scenarios.
Ed's comments: Delivered. For no-egress guarantees pair with network controls; happy to run the residency test together.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to A/B test model versions or providers on live traffic without application-layer changes, so that routing and procurement decisions are based on production evidence rather than benchmark claims or vendor marketing
Business Value / Rationale: Routing and procurement decisions are based on production evidence rather than benchmark claims or vendor marketing.
Acceptance Criteria: Administrators can split eligible live traffic between model/provider variants and measure results without application code changes.
Current Assessment: Route resolution is strictly first-match; no percentage split or experiment assignment exists.
SystemPrompt Fit: No percentage traffic splitting / experiment-assignment mechanism was evidenced.
Gap / Action Required: Implement experiment traffic splitting and measurement if A/B testing remains in scope.
Ed's comments: Moderate core change (split + assignment + measurement). P3 - propose deferring until a concrete A/B question exists.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to detect and redact PII/PHI in prompts and completions before they leave the org boundary or are persisted to logs, so that sensitive data exposure and regulatory violations are prevented at the gateway layer rather than relying on every application team to implement it independently
Business Value / Rationale: Sensitive data exposure and regulatory violations are prevented at the gateway layer rather than relying on every application team to implement it independently.
Acceptance Criteria: Configured sensitive-data categories are detected and redacted or blocked before external transmission and before persistence where required.
Current Assessment: 34 secret patterns + entropy backstop; PII email/credit-card + SSN/phone added this pass; display-layer redaction in admin transcripts.
SystemPrompt Fit: Email and credit-card detection/blocking are evidenced, but full PII/PHI coverage and completion-side redaction are not.
Gap / Action Required: Define enterprise PII/PHI taxonomy and implement complete request/response redaction or blocking.
Ed's comments: Enforcement blocks rather than redacts in flight; no PHI (health) taxonomy. Full redaction pipeline is a scoped design item - confirm required categories and redact-vs-block per category.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to enforce data residency by routing requests to region-specific or sovereign model instances based on data classification, so that customer or regulatory data never crosses a jurisdictional boundary it isn't permitted to cross
Business Value / Rationale: Customer or regulatory data never crosses a jurisdictional boundary it isn't permitted to cross.
Acceptance Criteria: Routing rules can enforce that classified workloads remain within the configured jurisdiction/region/sovereign endpoint.
Current Assessment: Supported
SystemPrompt Fit: Provider/model YAML carries governance metadata (european, no_retain); routes declare requires: blocks enforced at boot validation and at dispatch, with the requirement recorded on the audit row.
Gap / Action Required: Closed 2026-08-25: classification scheme decided as model-YAML governance booleans; core change landed (patch-active). Annotate any future EU/sovereign providers as european: true.
Validation Method: tests/integration/gateway req_037_residency + @REQ-037 Playwright spec (route requires round-trip)
Ed's comments: No first-class data-classification label forcing residency routing - enforcement is by convention. Provide the classification scheme and we add the routing predicate (pairs with REQ-038).

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to enforce that requests are only routed to model providers with a contractually agreed no-train / no-retain clause when handling classified data, so that submitted prompts and completions cannot be used by a provider to train or improve their models in violation of the org's data agreements
Business Value / Rationale: Submitted prompts and completions cannot be used by a provider to train or improve their models in violation of the org's data agreements.
Acceptance Criteria: Policy can prevent classified requests from being routed to providers that do not satisfy the configured no-train/no-retain contractual requirement.
Current Assessment: Supported
SystemPrompt Fit: governance.no_retain on providers (per-model override wins) + route requires: {no_retain: true}; a classified route cannot boot against, or dispatch to, a retaining provider.
Gap / Action Required: Closed 2026-08-25: contractual no-train/no-retain is provider metadata; local route claude-star-4203d1 demonstrates enforcement.
Ed's comments: Needs provider metadata + classification predicate in routing - pairs with REQ-037. Est 1-2 wks once the classification scheme lands.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to version and roll back prompts and system messages independently of application deploys, so that a prompt-level fix or regression can be corrected without requiring every consuming application to redeploy
Business Value / Rationale: A prompt-level fix or regression can be corrected without requiring every consuming application to redeploy.
Acceptance Criteria: Prompt/system-message versions are centrally versioned, deployable, auditable, and rollbackable independently of application release cycles.
Current Assessment: No prompt registry; nearest primitive (system-prompt overrides) has no version history - rollback today means redeploying the profile.
SystemPrompt Fit: Current source analysis indicates the older prompt/playbook versioning subsystem was removed; no first-class prompt rollback primitive is evidenced.
Gap / Action Required: Design a first-class prompt configuration/version lifecycle if independent rollback is required.
Ed's comments: Needs a first-class prompt lifecycle object (versioned, auditable, rollbackable). Design first; est 2-3 wks build after sign-off.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to centrally manage and distribute prompt templates across consuming applications, so that a security or quality fix can be applied once rather than requiring coordinated changes across every application team
Business Value / Rationale: A security or quality fix can be applied once rather than requiring coordinated changes across every application team.
Acceptance Criteria: Approved prompt templates can be centrally managed and distributed to consuming applications with controlled updates/revocation.
Current Assessment: Signed, centrally-revocable distribution exists (skills/plugins over Ed25519-signed manifests) and can carry prompt content today.
SystemPrompt Fit: Central signed-manifest distribution exists for skills/plugins, but prompt templates are not evidenced as a distinct first-class lifecycle object.
Gap / Action Required: Define whether prompt distribution will use skills or needs a dedicated prompt-template registry.
Ed's comments: Works as a distribution channel now; a versioned template object with parameters/pinning/rollback is the REQ-039 design. Recommend treating 039+040 as one piece of work.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to enforce permission, secret-exposure, and rate-limit checks on every tool call an agent makes before the underlying action executes, so that a misconfigured or compromised agent cannot take an unauthorized action just because it has model access
Business Value / Rationale: A misconfigured or compromised agent cannot take an unauthorized action just because it has model access.
Acceptance Criteria: Every agent/tool invocation passes required authorization, secret-exposure, safety, and rate-limit checks before the underlying action executes.
Current Assessment: 4-stage synchronous chain (scope check, secret scan, blocklist, rate limit) enabled this pass; first-deny-wins; every decision audited with trace linkage.
SystemPrompt Fit: Governance checks are enforced synchronously before dispatch and denied calls are audited.
Gap / Action Required: Validate every relevant tool path goes through pre-execution governance and audit.
Ed's comments: Enabled this pass (was built but deliberately off during evaluation). Run the negative tests in the evidence pack to confirm.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to register, authenticate, and govern every MCP server an agent can connect to, with a signed and centrally revocable allowlist, so that tool access for autonomous agents is controlled with the same rigor as model access
Business Value / Rationale: Tool access for autonomous agents is controlled with the same rigor as model access.
Acceptance Criteria: Every MCP server is centrally registered, authenticated, allowlisted, auditable, and revocable before agents can connect to it.
Current Assessment: Declarative MCP registry with per-server auth/scopes/audience, plan-based entitlement, immediate revocation, JTI token revocation.
SystemPrompt Fit: MCP allowlisting, authentication/scopes, auditability, and central revocation are evidenced.
Gap / Action Required: Validate MCP lifecycle operations, revocation propagation, and emergency kill-switch behavior.
Ed's comments: Delivered. Kill-switch = disable in YAML or suspend the org; both take effect immediately.

Detailed Requirement: As a Business, I shall be able to validate tool schemas at registration time, so that a malformed or incompatible tool integration fails at startup or deployment rather than failing during a live customer interaction
Business Value / Rationale: A malformed or incompatible tool integration fails at startup or deployment rather than failing during a live customer interaction.
Acceptance Criteria: Tool schemas are validated during registration/deployment and invalid or incompatible integrations fail before live runtime execution.
Current Assessment: Registration fails fast on missing/invalid manifests and DB schema sync; tool input schemas captured at discovery.
SystemPrompt Fit: Tool/schema validation at registration/connect time is evidenced so invalid integrations can fail before live execution.
Gap / Action Required: Test malformed/incompatible tool schemas in CI/deployment and verify fail-fast behavior.
Ed's comments: Caveat: no JSON-Schema meta-validation of tool contracts (a syntactically-valid-but-wrong schema passes). Add if malformed-schema CI tests are a hard requirement (~1 wk).
